messages:
Maya R.: :rotating_light: paging — multiple customers reporting 502/handshake failures hitting hosted API gateway since ~03:14 UTC
Simon L.: seeing spikes in tls handshake errors across frontends, routing ~80% errors to model endpoints, investigating
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03015-TLS-1 — severity: P1 — responders: @eng-oncall, @NetOps Bot — timeline started 2026-03-15T03:16:02Z
eng-oncall: I'm on it, collecting logs from edge LB and gateway. Can someone grab recent cert rotation job logs?
NetOps Bot: cert-rotation-job completed at 03:12:51Z on cluster-us-east-1, deployed cert bundle v2026-03-15-03 to gateways (sha256: a3f4...)
Alex P.: I can pull gateway logs and tcpdump on the LB. Pulling logs now — tailing /var/log/gateway/tls.log
Li Chen: quick customer impact check: preliminary list shows 12 active tenants with failures (some high QPS). CS-Support alerted customers with active sessions affected.
Oscar G.: curl to affected gateway returns TLS alert: 
```
$ curl -v https://api.us.redwood.ai/health
* SSL connect error
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
```
Maya R.: same from openssl s_client: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect api.us.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.us.redwood.ai
CONNECTED(00000003)
140735094275664:error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure:s23_clnt.c:770:
```
Simon L.: grabbing gateway verbose TLS traces — seeing SNI present, cert served is the new bundle but handshake aborts after server_hello in many cases.
eng-oncall: hypothesis 1: cert bundle incompatible with some client cipher suites (rotation introduced certificate chain ordering or altNames change). Hypothesis 2: MTU path issue causing TLS record fragmentation -> handshake fails. Hypothesis 3: VPC peering route flap causing TCP resets mid-handshake.
Li Chen: adding customer-observed errors: some show `connection reset by peer` at app-level followed by TLS alerts.
Alex P.: pasted tcpdump snippet (trimmed): 
```
03:13:58.123456 IP client > lb: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
03:13:58.123658 IP lb > client: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 28960
03:13:58.124001 IP client > lb: Flags [P.], seq 1, ack 1, length 512
03:13:58.124050 IP lb > backend: Flags [P.], seq 1, ack 1, length 512
03:13:58.124200 IP lb > client: RST, seq 1, win 0
```
Oscar G.: RST from LB right after forwarding TLS ClientHello — that's suspicious. Could be LB app-layer rejecting connection after inspecting cert.
NetOps Bot: noticed MTU change pushed to ENI config in us-east-1 at 03:11:48Z as part of network patch (mtu reduced from 9001->1500) — change targeted for CNNE cluster. Rollout started 03:11Z.
Maya R.: that MTU change coincides with cert rotation. Could be two simultaneous changes compounding. We need to test impact on large TLS records.
eng-oncall: mitigation plan attempt 1: disable new cert bundle on a subset of gateways (canary rollback) to see if clients recover. Rolling back for cluster-us-east-1-canary now.
Alex P.: rollback applied to 3/5 canary gateways at 03:20Z — still seeing some failures due to traffic balance, but error rate on those nodes drops ~80% for small-req clients.
Simon L.: MTU hypothesis test: forcing smaller TLS payloads (reduce initial SNI size padding) on test client — still see handshake fail on impacted path. Suggests MTU not sole cause.
eng-oncall: mitigation plan attempt 2: revert network MTU change on affected ENIs. NetOps, can you rollback mtu patch?
NetOps Bot: rolling back MTU change on CNNE cluster now (03:28Z). Reverting to 9001. Will monitor.
CS-Support: updated customers: "We're actively investigating TLS connectivity issues; mitigation in progress. No data lost; temporary request failures only."
Li Chen: monitoring dashboards: request success rate recovered to ~98% by 03:33Z after MTU rollback + cert rollback on canaries. Some residual errors on traffic through peered VPCs.
Alex P.: grabbed gateway debug log showing handshake path with error codes: 
```
[2026-03-15T03:22:11Z] tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: handshake failure, client_cipher: ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
[2026-03-15T03:22:11Z] tls: served cert fingerprint: a3f4... bundle v2026-03-15-03
```
Maya R.: running through tasks — need consolidated timeline and hypothesis tracker in this thread so RCA is straightforward.
Simon L.: timeline (quick): 03:11:48 MTU patch rollout starts (network), 03:12:51 cert-rotation-job completes, 03:14:00 first customer alerts, 03:16 incident created, 03:20 cert rollback on canaries, 03:28 mtu rollback started, 03:33 service success rate recovering.
eng-oncall: owners/actions: Alex P. — collect full gateway logs + filtered TLS handshakes per tenant; Li Chen — assemble impacted tenant list and severity; NetOps — provide mt logs and ENI events; Simon — reproduce handshake fail with controlled clients and record pcap; Maya — customer comms and timeline.
Oscar G.: running a reproducer against a node that still fails — capturing full pcap and `strace` of gateway worker to see if process is issuing RST.
Li Chen: customers with active persistent TLS (websocket/streaming) saw longer disruption; batch/short requests mostly recovered faster. Flagged two enterprise customers for follow-up.
eng-oncall: initial conclusion (in-incident): simultaneous MTU change + cert rotation correlated with broad handshake failures. Likely root cause: MTU change induced fragmentation of certain TLS records while a new cert bundle introduced slightly larger ServerHello/OCSP responses -> larger packets crossed a path with reduced MTU causing mid-handshake resets on some LBs and peered routes. Secondary factor: some peered VPC routes still using old ENI config causing asymmetric path MTU issues.
Maya R.: next steps: 1) full post-incident RCA doc (owner: Simon) 2) improve cert-rotation canary checks to include MTU/path MTU validations and handshake end-to-end tests (owner: Alex) 3) change control: do not perform network MTU changes during cert rotations (owner: NetOps) 4) create alert for sudden TLS handshake rate increase (owner: eng-sre).
Simon L.: I'll start the RCA doc and include the hypothesis matrix, logs, and pcap excerpts. Will schedule a follow-up review with NetOps and Security for cert chain sanity.
CS-Support: letting customers know we will follow up with root cause and remediation steps. Thanks all — closing incident once RCA doc is linked. :white_check_mark:
